extracted.intended_audience: journalism researchers, news industry analysts, policymakers, and media professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and metrics for evaluating the health of U.S. news media across audience, economic, newsroom, ownership and digital-traffic dimensions. Includes selection rules and methodological standards for measuring and comparing outlets and platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average weekday and Sunday newspaper circulation (print + digital)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average weekday and Sunday newspaper circulation, measured as print and digital combined, and reported as year-over-year percent change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report separate changes for weekday and Sunday circulation; note that declines can be driven entirely by print even if digital inches up. Watch for reporting-period changes (Alliance for Audited Media switched from six-month to three-month reporting in 2015) which affect comparability. Digital circulation includes both replica and non-replica editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of circulation that is digital
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of total circulation accounted for by digital editions (e.g., digital accounts for 22% of total circulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to assess how much print readership has migrated to digital; combine with absolute circulation trends to understand whether digital gains offset print losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising revenue — year-over-year change
rubrics_metrics.description: Total advertising revenue for newspaper (or other news-sector) companies and its percent change from the prior year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When industry-wide figures are unavailable, use revenue data from publicly traded newspaper companies as a proxy, but note limitations because these companies represent about a quarter of daily papers and revenue. Adjust for acquisitions/sales to keep the base of publications consistent when computing percent change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital advertising revenue share and trend
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of ad revenue coming from digital sources and the year-over-year change in digital ad revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both the share (e.g., one in four dollars) and whether digital ad revenue is growing or falling; interpret changes in context — a rising share may reflect print decline rather than digital growth. Use SEC filings where available for publicly traded companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circulation revenue (subscriptions/paid content) trend
rubrics_metrics.description: Year-over-year change in circulation revenue (subscriber revenue) for newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track separately from advertising revenue; may be stable even when ad revenue declines. Use consistent base of publications for comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net profit as indicator of cost-cutting success
rubrics_metrics.description: Net profit (or loss) for the company as an indicator of whether cost reductions are offsetting revenue declines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chart number of companies showing profit vs loss; note that net profit figures may include other business units (TV, websites) not solely the newspaper/publishing unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom employment (total and percent change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of full-time newsroom employees and year-over-year percentage changes (e.g., ASNE counts and declines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use American Society of News Editors Newsroom Employment Census for historic comparisons; watch for significant single-year drops (e.g., 10% declines). Break out by demographics (women, minority) where data exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce demographic composition and wage gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of newsroom employees who are women and minorities, and evidence of wage gaps by gender and race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both representation percentages and any documented pay disparities; use newsroom-level studies (e.g., Wall Street Journal/Dow Jones report) to illustrate common patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of daily newspapers (count and trend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of daily newspapers in the U.S. and changes over time (closures/launches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Editor & Publisher DataBook counts to document long-term declines in the number of daily papers (e.g., 1,331 in 2014 vs 1,457 in 2004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation and ownership changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Mergers, acquisitions, spinoffs, and other ownership changes among newspaper companies (e.g., Gannett, Tribune Publishing, E.W. Scripps / Journal Communications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document major consolidation events, bankruptcies, ownership opacity (e.g., undisclosed private investment groups), and antitrust concerns; include implications for newsroom resources and editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience source metrics — 'most helpful' source for news
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey measures of what source audiences find 'most helpful' for news (e.g., percent naming print newspapers vs TV, radio, social media, websites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public-opinion survey data (Pew surveys) to understand platforms' perceived usefulness; differentiate between 'most helpful' and any use in past week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique visitors (digital audience size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average monthly unique visitors to an outlet's website (desktop, mobile, and total digital population) as measured by comScore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match outlets to comScore total-domain entities when possible; report desktop and mobile separately and combined; note that unique visitors can dramatically outnumber circulation but include incidental visitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes per visit (engagement metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average minutes per visit (time spent) on a website or platform, measured monthly or as averages for an October-December quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report minutes per visit for desktop and mobile separately as well as total; use minute metrics to complement unique visitor counts because high traffic doesn't necessarily equal deep engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile vs desktop traffic comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in unique visitors and minutes per visit on mobile devices versus desktop (e.g., mobile visitors rising while mobile minutes per visit fall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a difference of 10% or more between desktop and mobile as significant (see significance rule). Use mobile trends to assess reach and engagement shifts among audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance threshold for desktop/mobile differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers considered the difference between a site's desktop and mobile monthly average unique visitors or average minutes per visit to be significant if one was at least 10% greater than the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this 10% rule when flagging meaningful differences between platform-specific metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratio of web traffic to print circulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of average monthly unique visitors to average Sunday circulation (e.g., web traffic may be 2 to 78 times greater than circulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ratio to highlight reach beyond subscribers; interpret carefully because many web visitors are one-time grazers rather than loyal readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion goal: grazing visitors to loyal readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The challenge/metric of converting incidental single-article web visitors into regular, loyal readers or subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure by tracking repeat visitation, subscription conversions, and time-spent patterns rather than unique-visitor counts alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comScore entity selection and vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of comScore entities representing outlets (prefer total-domain entities) and vetting with comScore analysts to remove entities with non-trendable/inorganic data shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When domain entities are incomplete, use custom total-domain entities; consider multiple entities resulting from site-structure changes as comparable; remove entries with likely inorganic measurement changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing months in comScore quarterly averages
rubrics_metrics.description: For sites that didn’t meet the reporting threshold for one month out of a quarter, researchers averaged across the two months with data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use two-month averages when a single month is missing to maintain comparability in quarterly comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for digital-native publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Four-part criteria to classify a site as digital-native: 1) born on the web (not legacy brand), 2) publishes original news content about current events with evidence of reporting, 3) not focused entirely on reviews/advice/raw data, 4) not primarily user-generated or aggregated content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess home page content for evidence of interviews, source documents, or a dedicated editorial staff; accept sites owned by legacy companies if 'born on the web' originally; exclude platforms like Medium, Reddit, Wikipedia and branded content hubs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection method for African American digital outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Maynard Institute’s annual list of black-oriented sites as an accounting of record and match those sites to comScore entities; exclude those without trendable data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report which sites were matched and note exclusions due to lack of trendable data (e.g., HuffPost BlackVoices excluded if no trendable data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of publicly traded companies as revenue proxy
rubrics_metrics.description: When industry-wide revenue data (e.g., NAA) are unavailable, use year-end SEC filings of publicly traded newspaper companies to estimate revenue trends, with adjustments for holdings and acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations: publicly traded companies represent about a quarter of daily papers; revenue used may be for entire company and include non-newspaper units; where possible, use revenue for only the newspaper/publishing unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments for acquisitions/sales in revenue comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: When a company acquired or sold publications over the course of a year, percent change was calculated using a revenue analysis that kept the number of publications constant from year to year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude companies from a year’s calculation if a consistent-base revenue change analysis was not provided by the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted viewership data for TV analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use weighted viewership data (newly available from Nielsen) to better account for the number of programming hours in a broadcast month when analyzing cable and network TV viewership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that weighted data may not differ substantially from unweighted data, and weighted median may be unavailable; document the change in methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: TV viewership metrics and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Nielsen audience data for cable (CNN, Fox, MSNBC), network morning and evening newscasts (ABC, CBS, NBC), and local TV market sweeps across four periods for affiliates of major networks, reporting prime-time/daytime/total daily viewership and timeslot-specific trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For local TV, include affiliates across all 210 U.S. media markets and four sweeps (Feb, May, July, Nov); account for anomalies like the 2009 March sweep due to digital transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retransmission and subscriber revenue metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure retransmission revenue and subscriber revenue for TV sectors (e.g., retransmission revenue expected to reach $6.3 billion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include as part of TV-sector economic health alongside ad revenues; track cyclical effects tied to election-year advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cord-cutting and subscription churn metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of the public who have turned away from cable or satellite TV subscriptions (cord-cutting prevalence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey measures to quantify cord-cutting (e.g., one-in-seven Americans) and interpret implications for pay-TV–dependent outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of digital ad revenue among top tech companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of total digital ad spending captured by a small number of technology companies (e.g., five companies capturing ~65%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use industry ad-spend estimates to show market concentration and potential impacts on news organizations’ revenue; consider desktop vs mobile ad distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'news' for inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational definition used for classifying publishers as news: 'current events affecting public life' including original reporting and commentary/analysis, with evidence on the homepage of reporting (interviews, eyewitness accounts, source documents) or self-description as news/journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this definition consistently when selecting digital-native publishers and when distinguishing news publishers from review/advice or branded-content sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of non-trendable or inorganic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities that showed increases or declines likely due to inorganic changes in measurement or site structure were considered to not have trendable data and were removed from analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vet unusual shifts with comScore analysts and exclude entities with measurement artifacts to preserve trend validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: PBS NewsHour funding breakdown as a sustainability indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of non-public funding sources for a public-broadcasting program (percent from foundations, corporations, individuals) and year-over-year change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funding mix (e.g., foundations rising to 71% of non-public funding) to assess financial vulnerability and diversification of revenue sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarter-over-quarter / year-over-year comparison window
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific time windows for comparisons (e.g., monthly averages of October-December 2014 vs October-December 2015) to measure year-over-year change in digital metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the comparison windows used and be consistent across outlets/sectors for comparability.
